What is well known among the scholars of the military campaigns (maghazi) and the biographies (siyar) is that this occurred during the expedition of al-Muraysi', which is the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq.

Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Ibn Ishaq: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, concerning the story of Banu al-Mustaliq: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was staying there, Jahjah ibn Sa'id al-Ghifari, who was a hired man of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Sinan ibn Wabr [in one copy: Sinan ibn Yazid] fought over the water. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban narrated to me, saying: They crowded at the water and fought. Sinan said: "O company of the Ansar!" Jahjah said: "O company of the Muhajirun!" Zayd ibn Arqam and a group of the Ansar were with 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. When he heard it, he said: "They have assaulted us in our land. By Allah, our situation and the situation of these Quraysh peasants is only as the saying goes: 'Fatten your dog and it will eat you.' By Allah, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it." Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said: "This is what you have done to yourselves: you have settled them in your land and shared your wealth with them. By Allah, if you had held back from them, they would have moved away from you to another land." Zayd ibn Arqam heard it and took it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was a youth; 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was with the Prophet ﷺ. He informed him of the report. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, order 'Abbad ibn Bishr to strike his neck." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Then how would it be, O 'Umar, when people say that Muhammad kills his companions? No, but call out, O 'Umar, for the departure."

When the news reached 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy that this had reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he came to him, apologized to him, and swore by Allah that he had not said what Zayd ibn Arqam attributed to him. He had standing among his people, so they said: "O Messenger of Allah, perhaps this boy made a mistake and did not establish exactly what the man said."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in the afternoon at an hour in which he did not usually travel. Usayd ibn al-Hudayr met him, greeted him with the greeting of prophethood, and then said: "By Allah, you have set out at a disagreeable hour, at which you never used to set out." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Has it not reached you what your companion Ibn Ubayy said? He claimed that when he comes to Medina he will expel the mightier from it, the weaker." He said: "You, O Messenger of Allah, are the mighty, and he is the weak one." Then he said: "O Messenger of Allah, be gentle with him, for by Allah, Allah has brought you, and we were stringing beads for him to crown him, for he sees that you have taken a kingship from him."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ traveled with the people until evening, through the night until morning, and continued through the day until the forenoon became intense. Then he halted with the people so as to occupy them away from what had been said. The people did not feel secure until they touched the ground and fell asleep. And Surat al-Munafiqun was revealed. [Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/290–292).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq informed us, Bishr ibn Musa informed us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a military campaign, and a man of the Muhajirun struck a man of the Ansar. The Ansari said: 'O Ansar!' and the Muhajiri said: 'O Muhajirun!' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What is this call of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance)? Leave it, for it is foul.'" 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, and they had done it: "By Allah, if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it." Jabir said: The Ansar were more numerous in Medina than the Muhajirun when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived; then the Muhajirun increased after that. 'Umar said: "Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions." [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (4/53).]

Imam Ahmad narrated it from Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. [Al-Musnad (3/392).] Al-Bukhari narrated it from al-Humaydi, and Muslim from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and others, from Sufyan, with similar wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4907; Sahih Muslim, no. 2584.]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Battle of Tabuk, when 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: 'If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it.'" He said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said: 'Then 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy swore that nothing of that had happened.'" He said: "My people blamed me and said: 'What did you intend by this?'" He said: "So I went away and slept, sorrowful and grieved." He said: "Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sent for me and said: 'Indeed Allah has revealed your excuse and confirmed you.'" He said: "Then this verse was revealed: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse"﴾ up to: ﴿If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it﴾."

Al-Bukhari narrated it at this verse from Adam ibn Abi Iyas, from Shu'bah. [Al-Musnad (4/368); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4902.] Then he said: "Ibn Abi Za'idah said, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ." Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it at this verse from the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same wording. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3314; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11594.]

Another route from Zayd: Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Adam and Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Israil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Arqam — and Ibn Abi Bukayr said, from Zayd ibn Arqam — say: "I went out with my paternal uncle on a military campaign, and I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul say to his companions: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, and if we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it.' I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me, and I related it to him. He sent for 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions, and they swore that they had not said it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ considered me a liar and believed them. A grief afflicted me such as had never afflicted me before, and I sat in the house. My uncle said: 'You intended nothing but that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would call you a liar and hate you.'" He said: "Until Allah revealed: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to me, then said: 'Indeed Allah has confirmed you.'" [Al-Musnad (4/373).]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 63, verses 5–8 (part 2 of 2):

Then Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, that he heard Zayd ibn Arqam say: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, and the people were afflicted with hardship. Abdullah ibn Ubayy said to his companions: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse from around him.' And he said: 'If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it.' So I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of that. He sent for Abdullah ibn Ubayy and questioned him, and he swore emphatically that he had not said it. They said: 'Zayd has lied, O Messenger of Allah.' So what they said weighed heavily on my mind, until Allah revealed my vindication: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called them so that he might ask forgiveness for them, but they turned their heads away." And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾. He said: "They were men of the most pleasing appearance."

This was narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i, through the narration of Zuhayr [[Musnad Ahmad (4/373), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4903), Sahih Muslim no. (2772), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11598).]]. Al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through the narration of Israil, both of them from Abu Ishaq, Amr [[In A: "from Abu Ishaq from Amr."]] ibn Abdullah al-Sab'i al-Hamdani al-Kufi, from Zayd, with the same wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4900) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3312).]].

Another chain from Zayd: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Israil, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'd [[In M: "Abu Sa'id."]] al-Azdi, who said: Zayd ibn Arqam narrated to us, saying: "We fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there were some Bedouins with us. We would race to the water, and the Bedouins would get ahead of us. A Bedouin would fill the pool for his companions, place stones around it, and set the leather mat over it until his companions arrived. A man from the Ansar came to the Bedouin, loosened the rope of his she-camel so that she could drink, but the Bedouin refused to let him. So he pulled out a stone, and the water flowed out. The Bedouin raised a piece of wood and struck the Ansari on the head, wounding him. He came to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, and informed him, and he was one of his companions. Abdullah ibn Ubayy became angry and said: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse from around him,' meaning the Bedouins. They used to attend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at mealtimes. Abdullah said to his companions: 'When they disperse from Muhammad's side, bring the food to Muhammad, so that he and those with him may eat.' Then he said to his companions: 'When you return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it.'" Zayd said: "I was riding behind my uncle, so I heard Abdullah and informed my uncle. He went and informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah sent for him, and he swore and denied it. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and called me a liar. My uncle came to me and said: 'You intended nothing but that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would hate you and the Muslims would deem you a liar.' So I was struck with a grief such as no one had ever experienced. While I was travelling with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, my head was drooping from worry, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me, pulled my ear, and smiled in my face. I would not have been pleased to have eternal life in this world in exchange for that. Then Abu Bakr caught up with me and said: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to you?' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said nothing to me, except that he pulled my ear and smiled in my face.' He said: 'Rejoice.' Then Umar caught up with me, and I told him the same as I had told Abu Bakr. When we reached the morning, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Munafiqun."

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Likewise, al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi narrated it from al-Hakim, from Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi, from Sa'id ibn Mas'ud, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, with the same chain. He added after the words "Surah al-Munafiqun": ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say: We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah﴾, until He said: ﴿They are the ones who say: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse﴾, until He said: ﴿The more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾ [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3313) and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (4/54).]].

Abdullah ibn Lahi'a narrated, from Abu al-Aswad, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, in the Maghazi (accounts of the campaigns), and likewise Musa ibn Uqba mentioned this story in his Maghazi with this same context. However, both of them said that the one who conveyed the words of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was actually Aws ibn Arqam, of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj. Perhaps this was another conveyer, or it was a mistake in hearing. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Aziz al-Ayli narrated to us, Salama narrated to us, Uqayl narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Muslim informed me, that Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and Amr ibn Tha'bit al-Ansari informed him: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went on the campaign of al-Muraysi', which was the one in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) destroyed the idol Manat, the tyrant, which was between Qafa al-Mushallal and the sea. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid, who broke Manat. During that campaign of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), two men fought: one of them was from the Muhajirun, and the other was from Bahz, who were allies of the Ansar. The man from the Muhajirun overpowered the man from Bahz. The Bahzi cried out: "O assembly of the Ansar!" Men from the Ansar came to his aid. The Muhajiri cried out: "O assembly of the Muhajirun!" Men from the Muhajirun came to his aid, until there was some fighting between those men of the Muhajirun and the men of the Ansar. Then they were separated, and every hypocrite (or: every man in whose heart was a disease) withdrew to Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and said: "You were expected to be a protection, and to repel [harm], but now you have become one who neither harms nor benefits. The peasants [jalabib] have aided one another against us." They used to call the newcomers from every migration "jalabib." Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the enemy of Allah, said: "By Allah, if we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it." Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, who was one of the hypocrites, said: "Did I not tell you: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse?" Umar ibn al-Khattab heard of this, so he came walking until he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to deal with this man who has troubled the people; let me strike his neck." He meant Abdullah ibn Ubayy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Umar: "Would you be the one to kill him if I commanded you to kill him?" Umar said: "Yes, by Allah, if you commanded me to kill him, I would strike his neck." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sit down." Then Usayd ibn al-Hudayr [[In M: "Hudayr."]], who was one of the Ansar and a member of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to deal with this man who has troubled the people; let me strike his neck." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Would you be the one to kill him if I commanded you to kill him?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, if you commanded me to kill him, I would strike him with the sword beneath his earlobes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sit down." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Announce the departure." So he set the people in motion in the heat of midday, and they travelled that day and night and the next day until the sun was high, then he halted. Then he set the people in motion again in the same manner, and they reached Medina in the morning after three days of travel from Qafa al-Mushallal. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, he sent for Umar and summoned him, and the Messenger of Allah said to him: "O Umar, would you have killed him if I had commanded you to kill him?" This is a strange chain of narration, and it contains valuable matters not found anywhere else.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada narrated to me that Abdullah ibn Ubayy, meaning when news reached him of what his father had done, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, it has reached me that you intend to kill Abdullah ibn Ubayy, because of what has reached you about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it, and I will bring you his head. By Allah, the Khazraj know that there was no man more dutiful to his father than I am. I fear that you will order someone else to kill him, and then my soul will not let me look at the killer of Abdullah ibn Ubayy walking among the people, and I would kill him, and so I would kill a believer for an unbeliever and enter the Fire." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat him well as long as he remains with us" [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/292).]].

Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned: When the people returned to Medina, this Abdullah ibn Abdullah stood at the gate of Medina, drew his sword, and people began passing by him. When his father Abdullah ibn Ubayy came, his son said to him: "Stay back." He said: "What is wrong with you? Woe to you!" His son said: "By Allah, you will not pass from here until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives you permission, for he is the mighty and you are the humble." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived, and he had been travelling at the rear of the caravan, Abdullah ibn Ubayy complained to him about his son. His son Abdullah said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, he will not enter it until you give him permission." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him permission, and he said: "Now that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has given you permission, pass through."

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated to us, Abu Harun al-Madani narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to his father: "By Allah, you shall never enter Medina until you say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the mighty and I am the humble." He said: He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, it has reached me that you intend to kill my father. By He who sent you with the truth, I have never looked at his face out of reverence for him. If you wish, I will bring you his head, for I will bring it to you. I dislike seeing the killer of my father" [[Musnad al-Humaydi (2/520).]]. \
